description: Stereo sample-rate reducer and bit crusher, with a resonant filter after them

params.text: Sets the rate the input is sampled and held at, 15000Hz fully anticlockwise down to 20Hz fully clockwise; the tooltip calls this Clock Frequency where the panel says Sample Rate
Sets how many bits each sample is rounded to, 16 fully anticlockwise through to 1 fully clockwise; at 16 the signal passes unrounded and at 1 it becomes a square between -5V and +5V
Blends the untouched input against the crushed and filtered signal
Sets the filter corner, 20Hz fully anticlockwise to 15000Hz fully clockwise, rising evenly with the knob; the tooltip reads a far lower frequency everywhere except the two ends
Sets the filter Q, 0.1 fully anticlockwise rising to 5.1 fully clockwise
Picks lowpass or highpass for the filter after the crusher
Scales the output, 0 to 100%, after the dry and wet are mixed

inputs.text: Shifts the sampling rate, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, clamped to ±5V before it is added
Shifts the bit depth by three bits per volt, clamped to ±5V before it is added
Shifts the dry and wet blend, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, clamped to ±5V before it is added
Shifts the filter corner, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, clamped to ±5V before it is added
Shifts the filter Q, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, clamped to ±5V before it is added
Shifts the output level, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, clamped to ±5V before it is added
Left audio in, and the signal used for both channels when the right jack is empty

outputs.text: The left channel crushed, filtered, blended and clamped to ±5V
The right channel crushed, filtered, blended and clamped to ±5V

notes: the rounding works on a window from -5V to +5V, so anything louder than that is flattened at those bounds before it reaches the filter.
